title: Top 5 Sunscreens for Your Body in 2026

children.text: If you only reach for sunscreen on beach days, your skin is missing out. Dermatologists recommend daily broad-spectrum protection on every exposed inch of skin, not just your face.
Every pick here is checked against testing data and reviews from sources like Consumer Reports and CNN Underscored before it makes the list. No rush, just really good picks.

products.name: Banana Boat Light As Air SPF 50
products.subtitle: best overall body sunscreen
products.blurb: This one has become a favorite among testers for feeling almost weightless on skin. It goes on with a matte finish and blends in cleanly across a range of skin tones without leaving the chalky white cast that plagues so many sunscreens.

products.name: Thrive Reef Safe Sunscreen SPF 50
products.subtitle: best reef-safe mineral sunscreen
products.blurb: If you spend time in the ocean or just want a simple ingredient list, this mineral formula relies on mineral UV filters rather than chemical ones, making it gentler for sensitive skin and reef-conscious for swimmers.

products.name: Sōl Labs Face and Body Sunscreen
products.subtitle: best all-around performer
products.blurb: Few sunscreens check every box dermatologists look for, but this one comes close: broad-spectrum coverage, water resistance, and reef-safe ingredients, all in one bottle for both face and body.

products.name: Coola Classic Body Sunscreen SPF 30
products.subtitle: best for dry or sensitive skin
products.blurb: This one leans into a lotion-like feel rather than a typical sunscreen texture, doubling as a light moisturizer with plant-derived antioxidants like raspberry seed and prickly pear extract.

products.name: Coppertone Pure & Simple Mineral Spray SPF 50
products.subtitle: best for sensitive skin
products.blurb: Built around zinc oxide, this fragrance-free formula skips common irritants like oxybenzone and parabens, a good option if you've reacted to chemical sunscreens before.

buyingTips: SPF 30+ is the general minimum for daily protection. Mineral sunscreens sit on top of skin and suit sensitive types; chemical sunscreens absorb in and often feel lighter. Reapply every 2 hours outdoors, or right after swimming or heavy sweating.
pullQuote: Still deciding? That's fine. We already did the slow part.

title: Top 5 Backpacks for Back to School in 2026

children.text: A backpack has to survive a full school year of being dropped, overstuffed, and dragged across campus — the bag that looks best on day one isn't always the one still holding together in May.
Every pick here is checked against reviews and testing data from sources like NBC Select, CNN Underscored, and Reviewed before it makes the list. No rush, just really good picks.

products.name: The North Face Borealis
products.subtitle: best dual-purpose backpack
products.blurb: This one holds up to both classroom routines and weekend hikes, with a stand-up shape, a padded laptop sleeve, and a removable waist strap for longer treks. Owners several years in report it's still holding together, which says more than any first-week impression can.

products.name: JanSport Main Campus
products.subtitle: best classic pick
products.blurb: A 32-liter main compartment and a dedicated organizer panel make this an easy fit for anyone who'd rather not think about where things go. It's been a reliable, unglamorous default for decades, and it still is.

products.name: Fjällräven Kanken Laptop 17"
products.subtitle: best for standing out
products.blurb: The boxy silhouette and padded 17-inch laptop sleeve make this one of the few backpacks that reads as a style choice rather than just a container. It costs more than the others here and comes in fewer colors, but the tradeoff is a bag people actually notice.

products.name: lululemon Everywhere Backpack
products.subtitle: best for a grown-up look
products.blurb: Water-repellent fabric and a clean, unbranded-looking shape mean this one transitions from high school hallways to an internship without looking out of place either way. Multiple interior pockets keep it organized without the bulk of a bigger bag.

products.name: Matein Extra Large Backpack
products.subtitle: best budget oversized pick
products.blurb: An affordable option that still manages padded, shoulder-friendly straps and enough room for a stack of textbooks and binders. It won't win style points, but it's a dependable choice for anyone who needs the space more than the branding.

buyingTips: A padded laptop sleeve is worth prioritizing if a device is coming along every day. Beyond that, wide, padded shoulder straps matter more over a full school year than extra pockets do — a bag carried daily should be judged on comfort first. Most day-to-day school needs fit in 20 to 32 liters; anything bigger starts to feel like a travel pack.
pullQuote: A good backpack outlasts the school year. A bad one gives up by October.

title: Tax-Free Weekend 2026: What to Buy and When

children.text: Most sales-tax holidays land in the summer, though the exact timing and what's exempt varies a lot by state — some run one weekend, others stretch into a full month. The categories below cover what's most commonly exempt, whatever's actually on your list.
Every pick here is checked against published state tax guidance before it makes the list, so you know roughly what's exempt and when to shop it. No rush, just really good timing.

products.name: Clothing & shoes
products.subtitle: the most universally exempt category
products.blurb: Nearly every participating state exempts everyday clothing and footwear up to some per-item price cap, which makes this the safest category to stock up on regardless of which state's holiday you're shopping.
products.examples: sneakers, jeans, lightweight jackets, everyday t-shirts

products.name: Electronics & home tech
products.subtitle: the big-ticket exemption, where it applies
products.blurb: Not every state's holiday covers electronics, and the ones that do usually cap the exempt price — so this is the category most worth double-checking against your specific state's rules before you assume a laptop or smart home gadget qualifies.
products.examples: everyday laptops, basic tablets, wireless earbuds, smart displays, home printers

relatedLinks.label: See our home tech gadget picks

products.name: Office & school supplies
products.subtitle: notebooks, pens, and bags, usually bundled together
products.blurb: Pens, notebooks, binders, and backpacks are typically grouped under one exemption with their own price cap, separate from the clothing cap — worth restocking whether or not anyone in the house is actually heading back to school.
products.examples: backpacks, notebooks, binders, pens and highlighters

products.name: Sporting goods & outdoor gear
products.subtitle: exempt in some states, taxed as usual in others
products.blurb: A few states extend the exemption to general sporting goods and outdoor equipment, while most don't — this is the category where it pays most to check your specific state's list rather than assume.
products.examples: sneakers and cleats, helmets, camping gear, swimwear

products.name: Energy- & water-efficient appliances
products.subtitle: a separate holiday in some states, worth timing around
products.blurb: A handful of states run a distinct energy- or water-efficiency tax holiday, sometimes the same weekend as the general one and sometimes on its own — worth checking if a larger appliance purchase is already on the calendar.
products.examples: Energy Star refrigerators, washing machines, water heaters, ceiling fans

buyingTips: Exemptions and price caps vary by state, so it's worth checking your own state's specific list before assuming a category qualifies. Buying online usually still counts as long as the order is placed and paid for during the window, even if delivery comes later — but check your retailer's tax settings to be sure it's applying the exemption correctly. The rates listed above are each state's base sales tax rate; many cities and counties add their own local tax on top, so actual savings may run higher.
pullQuote: A tax holiday won't make a bad purchase good. It'll just make it a little cheaper.

title: Top 5 Home Tech Gadgets Worth Having in 2026

children.text: Most "smart home" advice still assumes you want to automate an entire house at once. The gadgets that actually earn their keep tend to be smaller than that — one device that fixes one specific annoyance, set up in an afternoon and then forgotten about.
Every pick here is checked against reviews and testing data from sources like Engadget, Forbes Vetted, and TechRadar before it makes the list. No rush, just really good picks.

products.name: Amazon Echo Show 5 (3rd Gen)
products.subtitle: best all-around smart home hub
products.blurb: This one doubles as a home command center: check a video doorbell's feed, run through the day's calendar, and control lights or a thermostat by voice, all from a screen small enough not to dominate a kitchen counter. It plays well with most other ecosystems, which makes it an easy default for a first smart display.

products.name: Eufy Security Video Doorbell E340
products.subtitle: best for actually seeing packages
products.blurb: A second camera angled down at the doorstep means it actually catches what's happening at ground level, not just faces at eye height — useful for anyone tired of missing porch deliveries in the frame entirely. Local storage options also mean it can run without a mandatory subscription.

products.name: TP-Link Kasa Smart Plug
products.subtitle: best low-effort starting point
products.blurb: No smart bulbs or rewiring required — this one turns a regular lamp or fan into something schedulable and voice-controlled in about five minutes. Built-in energy monitoring is a nice bonus for anyone curious what's actually driving up the electric bill.

products.name: Anker Nebula Capsule 3 Laser
products.subtitle: most fun for the size
products.blurb: A soda-can-sized laser projector that throws a genuinely sharp 100-inch image and runs its own smart TV software, no streaming stick required. Battery life covers a full movie with no cord in sight, which is most of the appeal.

products.name: Govee M1 RGBIC LED Strip Light
products.subtitle: best ambiance upgrade
products.blurb: Individually addressable color segments mean it can shift through multiple colors at once instead of washing a room in one flat hue, and it can sync to music or whatever's on screen. Setup is stick-and-plug simple, with no separate hub required.

buyingTips: Check for Matter support before buying anything new — it's become the standard that lets devices from different brands work together without separate apps for each one. Beyond that, start with one or two gadgets that solve an actual annoyance rather than trying to automate the whole house at once; it's a much easier way to tell what's actually worth keeping.
pullQuote: A smart home doesn't have to be a whole system. Sometimes it's just one lamp that finally turns itself off.

title: Wireless Earbuds Under $100 That Don't Feel Cheap

children.text: Active noise cancelling used to be the thing that separated a $250 pair of earbuds from a $50 pair. That gap has mostly closed — the noise cancelling, battery life, and app tuning inside most sub-$100 earbuds now would have counted as flagship features a few years ago.
Every pick here is checked against reviews and testing data from sources like RTings, SoundGuys, and Wirecutter before it makes the list. No rush, just really good picks.

products.name: Soundcore Space A40 by Anker
products.subtitle: best overall pair under $100
products.blurb: This one keeps showing up near the top of independent noise-cancelling tests in its price range, and the app-based EQ and fit test make it easy to actually dial in — a rare case where the cheaper option doesn't feel like a downgrade.

products.name: Sony WF-C710N
products.subtitle: best noise cancelling from a name-brand
products.blurb: Sony's noise cancelling tuning tends to test well against much pricier earbuds, and this is the cheapest pair carrying it — a good pick for anyone who trusts an established audio brand over a newer one.

products.name: Soundcore Liberty 4 NC by Anker
products.subtitle: best battery life
products.blurb: A 50-hour total battery rating with the case, plus wireless charging, makes this the pair least likely to run out mid-week. It also supports hi-res audio codecs that most sub-$100 earbuds skip entirely.

products.name: JBL Tune Buds
products.subtitle: best for calls and bass
products.blurb: JBL's signature bass-forward tuning is still here, but the bigger upgrade is call quality — multiple mics per earbud cut down on the wind and background noise that usually gives budget earbuds away on a call.

products.name: TOZO T10
products.subtitle: best ultra-budget pick
products.blurb: One of the best-reviewed earbuds on Amazon for years running, and still under $20 most of the time. It skips noise cancelling entirely, but for anyone who just wants reliable sound and a case that survives a bag, it's hard to beat the price.

buyingTips: Active noise cancelling is the biggest jump in this price range, but it isn't free — it trades some battery life and usually adds a few dollars, so skip it if you mostly listen at a desk. Ear tip size matters more than the spec sheet for how these actually sound; most brands include 3–4 tip sizes, and the wrong fit is the single most common source of "this bass sounds weak" complaints.
pullQuote: Nobody needs $250 earbuds to hear a podcast at 1.5x speed.

title: Portable Fans That Won't Die Halfway Through Summer

children.text: "Portable fan" covers a lot of very different objects — a handheld fan for a commute, a neck fan for yard work, and a battery-powered tower fan for a bedroom aren't really substitutes for each other. So this isn't a ladder from best to worst. It's five different problems, each paired with the fan built to handle it.

Every pick below is checked against its real purchase and review history before it makes the list — a rating only means something once it holds up across a large volume of buyers, not a handful of five-star reviews on a brand-new listing.

products.name: Shark FlexBreeze 2-in-1 Pedestal and Tabletop Fan
products.subtitle: the pick if you only want one fan
products.blurb: Shark's name recognition alone sets this apart from most of the category, and the fan backs it up — it converts between a full pedestal and a tabletop unit, runs corded or cordless for up to 24 hours, and is rated for both indoor and outdoor use. It won't fit in a bag like the others on this list, but it's the closest thing here to an all-purpose replacement for a house fan.

products.name: DREO Tower Fan for Bedroom
products.subtitle: best for quiet all-day cooling
products.blurb: DREO has built a real reputation in home cooling over the last few years, and this tower fan is a good example why — 28dB at its quietest setting is genuinely bedroom-friendly, and the 90° oscillation covers a room without needing to be repositioned every hour.

products.name: JISULIFE 3-in-1 Portable Fan
products.subtitle: best budget grab-and-go pick
products.blurb: JISULIFE isn't a big-box name, but it's the closest thing to one inside the portable fan category specifically — this exact model has tens of thousands of reviews holding steady at 4.6 stars. It doubles as a phone power bank and a flashlight, which makes it an easy one to toss in a bag and forget about until it's needed.

products.name: FrSara Neck Fan
products.subtitle: best hands-free pick
products.blurb: Hands-free cooling for anyone doing yard work, walking a dog, or standing in line outdoors. It blows air from both sides of the neckband instead of just one, and the low-profile design is built specifically to avoid catching on long hair — a common complaint with cheaper neck fans.

products.name: Koonie 8" Clip-on Fan
products.subtitle: best for strollers, desks, and tight spaces
products.blurb: A sturdy clamp and a real 10,000mAh battery separate this from the flimsier clip fans that show up in the same search results. It holds onto a stroller rail, a treadmill console, or a desk edge without sliding, and the airflow is noticeably stronger than its size suggests.

buyingTips: Speed settings on the box are marketing — battery-powered fans vary a lot more in actual airflow than the "5 speeds" label suggests, so runtime and reviewed airflow matter more than the spec sheet. A bigger battery (measured in mAh) roughly tracks with how long a fan lasts on its highest setting, which is usually the one people actually pick. Outdoor misting fans need a water refill and aren't on this list for that reason — they're a different category from a straight battery fan.
pullQuote: No fan has ever fixed summer. It just makes summer stop yelling at you.
